solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Irritation card game is cut short

indicators.note: A word cut short loses its end.

parts.note: piquet is an old two-player card game

explanation.surface: A card game gets abandoned halfway, much to the players' annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: PIQUET is a seventeenth-century card game for two; lop off its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is a feeling of irritation or resentment, especially from wounded pride.

clue.text: Childish anger follows regular helpings of prunes

indicators.note: The word for anger comes after the letters taken from 'prunes'.
Helpings taken at regular intervals from 'prunes' are its first, third and fifth letters.

parts.note: P, U and E are the odd letters of PRUNES
to rile is to anger

explanation.surface: A small child throws a tantrum at being served prunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anger' is a verb here: RILE, not a noun like IRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: puerile comes from Latin puer, a boy, so it means behaving like a child.

clue.text: Perhaps survey and search island on new river in Yorkshire

parts.note: a quest is a search
I is the abbreviation for island
used as itself
N is the abbreviation for new
the Aire flows through Leeds

explanation.surface: Surveyors comb an island in a newly charted Yorkshire river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aire is a river in Yorkshire, northern England, running through Leeds. 'Perhaps' flags that a survey is only one kind of questionnaire.
explanation.definitionFit: A survey is one example of a questionnaire, a set of questions put to many people.

clue.text: Illegal use of force breaking down exit — or not?

indicators.note: Something breaking down falls apart, so the letters of 'exit or not' come apart and re-form.

parts.note: used as itself
used as itself

explanation.surface: Someone muses about forcing a way out of a door that will not open.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash and question mark hide that 'or not' is part of the letters to rearrange, not a musing aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Extortion is obtaining something, usually money, by force or threats.

clue.text: Run small van for living in on holiday

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small

parts.words: van for living in on holiday
parts.note: a camper van is fitted out for holiday living

explanation.surface: Someone operates a small campervan for holidaymakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like 'operate' in the surface, but it is the definition, in the sense of dashing about.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to run with quick, light steps.

clue.text: Short trip that is taken after class

indicators.note: 'That is' is placed after the word for class.

parts.note: a sort is a class or kind
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: Pupils go on a quick outing once lessons are over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' reads as a school lesson, but it means a kind or category.
explanation.definitionFit: A sortie is a short trip away from base, originally a military raid.

clue.text: Champion in speed contest losing lead

indicators.note: The lead is the first letter.

parts.note: a race is a contest of speed

explanation.surface: A champion falls behind in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing lead' pretends to be about a runner falling back; it removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: an ace is someone who excels at something, a champion in their field.

clue.text: We finally give thought to cutting dance for greater number

parts.note: to prance is to dance about

indicators.note: 'We finally' is the last letter of 'we'.

parts.note: the last letter of WE
to ponder is to think about

explanation.surface: Someone at last considers dropping a dance so as to reach more people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' reads as dropping the dance, but here it means slicing into it; 'We finally' is just the one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A preponderance is a greater number or amount of one thing than another.

clue.text: Ceremony set down on paper as it is said

indicators.note: The word for 'set down on paper' is spoken, not spelt.

parts.note: to write is to set down on paper

explanation.surface: A ceremony's words are recorded exactly as spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: WRITE and RITE sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a rite is a formal ceremony, as in last rites or a rite of passage.

clue.text: Clergyman is after English builder

indicators.note: The clergyman comes after the abbreviation for English.

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A vicar is pursuing an English builder.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards: the clergyman is written after English.
explanation.definitionFit: An erector is someone who erects or builds something.

clue.text: Definitely not odd temperature leading to incident

parts.note: a number that is not odd is even
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A perfectly normal temperature sets off an incident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Definitely not odd' reads as 'quite ordinary' but means an even number.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both words name something that happens, a single occurrence.

clue.text: Reshuffled minister is on break

indicators.note: A reshuffle mixes things up, so the letters of 'minister is on' are reordered.

parts.note: used as itself

explanation.surface: A minister moved in a cabinet reshuffle is now on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: A reshuffle is when a prime minister moves ministers between jobs; here it rearranges letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An intermission is a break, especially between parts of a show.

clue.text: Right person of brilliance to lead directors

indicators.note: The star goes first, leading the board.

parts.note: a star is a brilliant performer
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: The right brilliant person is found to chair a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like 'suitable' but is the ship's side.
explanation.definitionFit: Starboard is the right-hand side of a ship facing forward.

clue.text: Uncovered text, both nice and strange

indicators.note: Uncovering strips each word's outer letters, leaving the middle.

parts.note: TEXT without its outer letters
BOTH without its outer letters
NICE without its outer letters

explanation.surface: A revealed text turns out to be pleasant and odd at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both' looks like a joining word pairing 'nice and strange', but it is fodder too.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotic means strikingly strange or unusual.

clue.text: Carriage catch with gold on

indicators.note: Gold is put on, added after the catch.

parts.note: to land a fish is to catch it
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A carriage door has a gilded catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' looks like a door fastening but is the verb, as in landing a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding top.

clue.text: With no way of proving age, is not taken out

definitions.text: With no way of proving age
definitions.meaning: a document with no date written on it gives no way to tell how old it is
someone never taken out on a date

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is someone never taken out on a date.
explanation.definitionFit: Something undated bears no date to show its age; someone undated has never been asked out.

clue.text: Poison remedy includes stripped bark

parts.note: a cure is a remedy
BARK without its outer letters

explanation.surface: An antidote to poison is made from stripped tree bark.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, curare really is made from plant bark and stems.
explanation.definitionFit: Curare is a paralysing plant poison once used on South American arrow tips.

clue.text: "Been curd" menu got wrong — not checked

indicators.note: Letters got wrong are out of their proper order.

parts.note: used as itself
used as itself

explanation.surface: A menu misprints 'bean curd' as 'been curd', and nobody proofread it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not checked' looks like 'not proofread' but means not held back.
explanation.definitionFit: Unencumbered means free of hindrance, not checked or restrained.

clue.text: It follows the herd up street, first of all

indicators.note: The first letter of all the words 'the herd up street' is taken.

parts.note: the initials of THE, HERD, UP, STREET

explanation.surface: Something trails a herd of cattle being driven up a street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It follows' looks like the start of the scene, a creature behind the herd, but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Thus' marks a conclusion: it follows that.

clue.text: The man's getting time for robbery

parts.note: the man's = he is
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A man is sent to prison for a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is a contraction, 'the man is', not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: heist is slang, originally American, for a daring robbery, typically of a bank or jewels.

clue.text: Gallery disposing of European rubbish

parts.note: the Tate is the London art gallery
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A gallery clears out junk from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of British national art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: Tat is British slang for cheap, tasteless rubbish.

clue.text: Not in favour of a City way when grasping profit

parts.note: used as itself
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way in a city
gain is profit

explanation.surface: Someone disapproves of the City of London's grasping approach to making money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The City' is London's financial district, so its 'way' sounds like its culture; here it is just a street.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: as a preposition, against means opposed to, the opposite of 'for'.

clue.text: The woman gets warm in cover

parts.note: the woman = she
to heat is to warm

explanation.surface: A woman keeps warm under a blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' is a verb here, to put something in a sheath, which is why the answer ends in E.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe is to cover, as a sword is put in its sheath.

clue.text: Really don't look forward to days with book, say

parts.note: d. is the standard abbreviation for day, here standing for days
a good book is a read; 'say' marks the example

explanation.surface: Someone is not looking forward to long days stuck with a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A read' is a noun for something to read, so a book is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to dread is to anticipate something with great fear, the strong opposite of looking forward to it.
